question.knowledge_point: Finding a Derivative Using Properties of Inverse Functions
question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=\sqrt{2x-1}.$ Given that $y=f(x)$ is invertible throughout its domain, determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3).$
question.worked_solution:
To determine $({f}^{-1})^{′}(3),$ we use the following formula:

$$
{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3)=\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))}
$$

First, we calculate the value of ${f}^{-1}(3).$ To do this, we solve the equation ${f}^{-1}(3)=x.$ For $x>\frac{1}{2}$, this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(3) & =x \\ f(x) & =3 \\ \sqrt{2x-1} & =3 \\ 2x-1 & =9 \\ 2x & =10 \\ x & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${f}^{′}(5),$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =\sqrt{2x-1} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x-1}} \\ {f}^{′}(5) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\cdot 5-1}} \\ {f}^{′}(5) & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(5)} \\  & =\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
